brief: The canvas displays typographic elements initially arranged in rigid, structured black and white grids, reminiscent of classic exhibition posters. However, this formality is unstable; the characters and lines begin to melt away from their precise grid positions. These elements are in constant, dynamic flux, reforming into fluid, organic shapes driven by visible mechanical mechanisms like gears and cams. The overall composition appears to breathe and reshape itself, transitioning between structured order and chaotic, liquid form without requiring any external input.

statement: This sketch explores the tension between rigid structure and fluid transformation, depicting typographic elements that appear to breathe and reshape themselves. The composition begins as a formal grid of text—reminiscent of classic Swiss design principles—but gradually dissolves into organic motion through subtle sine wave oscillations. Each character element shifts position and rotates independently, creating an impression of mechanical forces at work without explicit machinery. The visual effect captures the essence of systems that exist in a state of constant flux between order and chaos, where the underlying structure remains but its manifestation continuously evolves.
